axes.model_access:
**Multi-vendor models, switchable inside the CLI.**

Official README wording:

**Official wording**: "By default, `copilot` utilizes Claude Sonnet 4.5. Run the `/model` slash command to choose from other available models, including Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-5"

The official changelog's GA wording was:

**Official wording**: "Choose from the latest models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google"

**Note the two official pages describe the default model differently**:

- the README says Claude Sonnet 4.5
- the about page says "The default model used by GitHub Copilot CLI is Claude Sonnet 4. GitHub reserves the right to change this model"

**The exact list of available models varies by plan**; the full list is on the Copilot models page (same account system as the [IDE entry](./copilot.md)).

Third-party agent delegation follows Copilot platform capabilities (Preview).
axes.runtime:
**A local terminal process**, lifecycle bound to the terminal session.

Officially supported systems:

- Linux
- macOS
- Windows: via Powershell or Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)

Official wording on support:

**Official wording**: "Linux / macOS / Windows from within Powershell and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)"

The about page adds:

**Official wording**: "Native Windows support in Powershell is available, but experimental"

**There is also a cloud execution surface.** `copilot --cloud` starts a session in an isolated cloud-hosted environment (official docs say cloud sandboxes are "in public preview", their policies "inherit from Copilot cloud agent policies", sessions can continue across machines and run tasks in parallel).

**These are two execution surfaces — the local terminal session and the cloud one; do not conflate them.**
axes.local_files:
**Bounded by "trusted directories".** When starting a session, the official docs require you to "confirm that you trust the files in, and below, the directory from which you launched the CLI".

This trusted directory controls **"where Copilot CLI can read, modify, and execute files"**.

**Key caveat**: the official docs state plainly

**Official wording**: "Scoping of permissions is heuristic and GitHub does not guarantee that all files outside trusted directories will be protected"

**Do not treat trusted directories as a hard sandbox.**

For a harder boundary, enable the local sandbox: **Official wording**: "run `/sandbox enable` inside a session", which restricts filesystem, network and system capabilities. Or use `copilot --cloud` to put the whole session in a cloud-isolated environment.
axes.background:
**There is explicit background delegation and cloud sessions.** Official changelog wording:

**Official wording**: "Prefix any prompt with `&` to delegate work to the Copilot coding agent in the cloud, freeing your terminal for other tasks. Use `/resume` to switch between local and remote coding agent sessions seamlessly"

That is, **in the terminal you hand the task to the cloud coding agent and keep using the terminal for other things.**

Cloud sandboxes (public preview) additionally support:

**Official wording**: "keep a session's state between uses, continue a session from a different machine, or run multiple tasks in parallel"

**The local session itself still ends with the terminal.** It is a client-resident type; the real background comes from the cloud channel above.
axes.tools:
**MCP is a default capability.** Official README wording:

**Official wording**: "the coding agent ships with GitHub's MCP server by default and supports custom MCP servers"

How to add: `/mcp add` for interactive adding; `/mcp search` browses the GitHub MCP Registry for direct install (2026-06-23 changelog).

Other extension surfaces listed in official docs:

- **Custom instructions**
- **Custom agents** — including built-in Explore / Task / Code Review / Plan specialist agents, runnable in parallel
- **Hooks**
- **Skills**
- **Plugins**

There is also **LSP**: you install language servers yourself, configured via `~/.copilot/lsp-config.json` or `.github/lsp.json`.

**ACP integration is supported** (the official concepts page has a "Use Copilot CLI via ACP" section; the changelog mentions ACP closeSession).

On macOS / Windows, local sessions can additionally enable **computer use** to operate desktop apps.
axes.context:
**The trio: auto-compaction + session management + repository memory.**

Auto-compaction: official docs say when a session nears the **95%** token limit, "Copilot automatically compresses your history in the background", enabling "virtually infinite sessions".

Manual operations: `/compact` compacts manually; `/context` shows token usage.

Rollback uses `/rewind`. The changelog says it

**Official wording**: "no longer requires git and restores only the files Copilot changed, skipping any file whose contents no longer match what Copilot last wrote"

and optionally **Official wording**: "conversation-only or conversation + files".

Cross-session memory follows **Copilot Memory** (the same feature as the [IDE entry](./copilot.md) in this section, storing repo-level conventions and preferences).
axes.permissions:
**Approval is the axis most worth remembering in this entry, with finer granularity than the IDE form.**

On first use of write / executable tools, the official docs give three options:

- 1. Yes
- 2. Yes, and approve TOOL for the rest of the running session
- 3. No, and tell Copilot what to do differently (Esc)

Official wording:

**Official wording** (the three approval-prompt options): "1. Yes" / "2. Yes, and approve TOOL for the rest of the running session" / "3. No, and tell Copilot what to do differently (Esc)"

**Option 2 means all commands of that tool class are allowed for this session.** Official example: after approving `rm ./this-file.txt`, any `rm` can run in the session.

Programmatic / unattended mode has three switches:

- `--allow-all-tools` — never ask for any tool
- `--allow-tool` — allow specified tools
- `--deny-tool` — forbid specified tools, **highest priority**

Values support "`shell(COMMAND)`, `write`, `MCP_SERVER_NAME`", and **`--deny-tool` takes precedence over `--allow-tool` / `--allow-all-tools`**.

The official warning about auto-approval is worth remembering verbatim:

**Official wording**: "Copilot has the same access as you do to files on your computer, and can run any shell commands that you can run, without getting your prior approval"

The official docs also recommend using auto-approval inside VMs / containers / offline environments to limit blast radius.

For content exclusion, the CLI for Business / Enterprise users:

**Official wording**: "respects content exclusion policies configured at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels"

Enterprise and organization policies can disable the CLI entirely.
axes.fit:
Fits three kinds of people:

- those already in the GitHub ecosystem who want to finish "read the repo / edit code / run tests / open PRs / manage issues" from the terminal — the official use cases literally include tasks like "create a pull request on GitHub.com"
- those who need **scripting / headless** (`copilot -p` with approval options can run in CI)
- those who need the MCP / plugins / custom-agent ecosystem

**Not a fit** for two kinds of people:

- those unwilling to pay for a Copilot subscription — the CLI comes with the subscription and cannot be bought separately
- those wanting "fully automatic yet zero risk" — auto-approval must be paired with an isolated environment; the official docs flag the risk explicitly

sections.与 IDE 形态的差别（只说差异）:
| Dimension | IDE form (see ./copilot.md) | CLI form (this entry) |
|---|---|---|
| Entry | editor / website | terminal `copilot` |
| Non-interactive | generally none | **`copilot -p` / `--prompt`**, usable in scripts and CI |
| Approval | editor modes | **terminal three-option prompt + `--allow/--deny-tool` switches** |
| Cloud execution surface | website / coding agent | `copilot --cloud` cloud sandbox (public preview) |

**Shared parts are not repeated**: model lists, Copilot Memory, org policies all follow the [IDE entry](./copilot.md); plan pricing always goes to the official plans page.
sections.程序化与安装:
Installation is primarily via the npm package. The official prerequisite is `Node.js 22 or later`:

```
npm install -g @github/copilot
```

There are also WinGet (`winget install GitHub.Copilot`), Homebrew (`brew install --cask copilot-cli`) and an install script.

Besides `/login`, authentication supports a **fine-grained PAT with the "Copilot Requests" permission**, placed in `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

**Official example**: `copilot -p "Show me this week's commits and summarize them" --allow-tool='shell(git)'`

Add `-s` to output only the answer, omitting usage info.
sections.权限与审批（本条目最值得记的一维）:
The three-option approval prompt (official wording):

```
1. Yes
2. Yes, and approve TOOL for the rest of the running session
3. No, and tell Copilot what to do differently (Esc)
```

**Option 2 means more than it reads.** Official example: after approving `rm ./this-file.txt`, any `rm` (e.g. `rm -rf ./*`) can run in the session. This is "allow by tool class", not per-command approval.

Unattended mode uses three switches, and **deny wins**:

| Switch | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--allow-all-tools` | never ask for any tool |
| `--allow-tool` | allow specified tools |
| `--deny-tool` | **forbid specified tools, highest priority** |

Values support `shell(COMMAND)` (down to the `shell(git push)` level), `write`, `MCP_SERVER_NAME`.

Official warning: with `--allow-all-tools`, it has the same local access as you.

Local files and commands all count, with no per-item confirmation.

The official docs recommend using it in VMs / containers / offline environments to limit blast radius.

**Trusted directories are not a hard sandbox.** The official docs state plainly that the boundary

> "is heuristic and GitHub does not guarantee that all files outside trusted directories will be protected"
sections.额度：按提示词扣 premium requests:
Each prompt costs one premium request. Official wording:

> Each time you submit a prompt to Copilot CLI, your monthly quota of Copilot premium requests is reduced by one.

Non-default models multiply by the model rate (e.g. Claude Opus 4.5 is 3x).

The Free tier officially allows up to 50 premium requests per month. Paid tiers' built-in models (GPT-5 mini / GPT-4.1 / GPT-4o) do not consume quota.

The official docs also announced that starting 2026-06-01, Copilot moves from request-based billing to usage-based billing.

Plan pricing is on the official plans page (per this site's D9 rule, no prices are stored here).
sections.核验说明:
Basis for `confidence: partial`: execution modes and approval options were obtained. MCP / extension surfaces were also obtained.

Context management and billing units were also obtained.

Sources are official docs and the official repository.

**The remaining gap is mainly "the exact mapping between the CLI and each Copilot plan".** The official about page lists Pro/Pro+/Business/Enterprise, while the quickstart page says all Copilot plans — the two pages are inconsistent. Per this site's iron rule this is recorded as "not stated by the official docs", listing the pages checked, without picking one on the vendor's behalf.
